sources.citation: Wurm, Stephen A. 2007. Australasia and the Pacific. In Moseley, Christopher (ed.), Encyclopedia of the World's Endangered Languages. London: Routledge. Entry 'Arafundi-Enga Trade Pidgin', p.472.
sources.note: Nothing. Seven-line encyclopedic entry: location (East Sepik/Enga Provinces), 'a simplified Enga with significant lexical input from Arafundi. It contains some structural features which belong to neither of these two languages', vitality. No phonology at all.

sources.citation: Wurm, S.A., Mühlhäusler, P. & Tryon, D.T. (eds.) 1996. Atlas of Languages of Intercultural Communication in the Pacific, Asia, and the Americas, Vol. II: Texts (chapter on Sepik trade languages / Papuan-based pidgins). Berlin: Mouton de Gruyter.
sources.note: Contains a paragraph on Arafundi-Enga pidgin ('some structural features cannot be derived from either language'); the full passage might mention phonology. Secondary, based on Williams.

sources.citation: Williams, Jeffrey P. 1995. A note on the pronominal system of Arafundi-Enga Pidgin. Journal of Pidgin and Creole Languages 10(1): 171-175.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only first-hand published description of the pidgin; pp.172-175 unread. Low probability of a prosody remark (it is a pronoun note), but it is the sole primary text and would settle whether any phonological comment exists.

sources.citation: Williams, Jeffrey P. 1993. Documenting the Papuan-based pidgins of insular New Guinea. In Byrne & Holm (eds.), Atlantic Meets Pacific, 355-367. Amsterdam: Benjamins (CLL 11).
